DSH LAUNCH PLANNER — issue #226 task 8.8 part (d) Pass B: ONE surviving security medium. Branch slice-dsh-planner-d at HEAD d65f0784; adopt every commit. Narrow scope: R1, plus one LOW.

WHERE THIS STANDS. Run dsh-launch-planner-issue-226-tas-3d08ce19 delivered Pass B's admission (one separate-value --model, the shared effort forms, one exact --patch, every residual refused, fixed diagnostics that echo nothing) and repaired the original-adjacency and storage-diagnostic findings of its first council. Its chief validated fmt, workspace clippy, the crate suites, OpenSpec and both bundle compiles. It then parked REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-MEDIUM on the one finding below. That parked run stays as it is for the operator; this run repairs the finding.

R1 — MEDIUM, security and correctness, verbatim from that chief: crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs:760-763 still deletes a LEADING payload `--` after Clap has consumed the outer separator. Thus `brokkr driver dsh -- --` and `brokkr driver dsh -- -- --model p/m` become admissible instead of refusing the residual terminator before provider work. Reproduced on disabled, enabled-cold and offered paths with an owned harmless shim: all six launched a child with a staged overlay, allocated a retained root and emitted three checkpoints; cold/offered also probed the version. Six comparison cases containing a SURVIVING terminator refused by the fixed option-terminator reason with zero probes, children, retained roots and checkpoints. With a bound absent route, a leading terminator reaches route-file resolution on all three paths while a trailing terminator refuses first. The unit expectation at crates/brokkr-cli/src/tests.rs:1186-1191 CODIFIES the deletion and must flip; built-driver coverage omits the leading case.

THE RULE, not the instance. After Clap parsing, the DSH adapter's admission must see EVERY payload token exactly as given — no stripping, leading, trailing or interior. Find every site in brokkr-cli that removes or normalises a `--` from a driver payload (lib.rs:747-763 and :2767 were both named across the two councils) and decide each by what the OTHER adapters rely on: their behaviour must not change, and that must be shown by their existing tests staying green, not asserted. If the stripping is shared, make the DSH path opt out of it rather than changing the shared path. Prove leading-, interior- and trailing-terminator refusal through the BUILT CLI on all three paths (disabled, enabled-cold, offered), each with zero provider observations: no version probe, no child, no staged overlay, no retained root, no checkpoint. Prove by removal: restore the stripping, name the failing test and assertion, restore the fix.

R2 — LOW, same chief: crates/brokkr-cli/tests/driver_conformance.rs:310-319,340-341 derives the new fixture's workdir, shim, marker, DSH_HOME and operator HOME from raw tempfile paths. Canonicalise each temporary root once before deriving those paths (macOS: /var is a symlink to /private/var).

A FACT ABOUT THIS RECIPE, stated so nobody spends a finding on it again: the verify gate is an exec step of the recipe that runs `cargo test --workspace`; no seat chooses or can change that invocation, and the controller owns it (issue #255). The smith's own validation is what this commission scopes: crate-scoped and sequential.

RULES. Assert reasons, never is_err(). Diagnostics echo no option name, value, model, ID or path. No Windows handling (decision 0063). GATES for the smith, crate-scoped and sequential: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; each crate's suite on its own; openspec validate --all --strict; both bundle compiles.

OUT OF SCOPE: Pass C (launch-root confirmation), 9.6, 10.x, 11.x, groups 14–15, any live provider call. DO NOT TICK 8.8 or 8.10. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/, extensions/dsh/, docs/decisions/ do not move; the DSH route stays disabled. Record what you delivered and what Pass C still owes.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

result.notes: Framing: .forge/tasks/dsh-pass-b-terminator.md. Confirmed HEAD d65f0784. R1 repairs a shared CLI separator-stripping bypass of the existing DSH admission rule; R2 canonicalizes test roots. The security medium and cross-adapter regression risk warrant a review panel, without new contract design or core/store/policy changes. Framed built-CLI refusal on all three paths, zero provider observations, removal proof and sequential validation. No implementation or tests performed.

R1 (MEDIUM) and R2 (LOW) closed on slice-dsh-planner-d at d65f0784; delivered as e23c11ef (code) and df74ca35 (tasks record), both signed, nothing pushed. R1: clap consumes the outer separator itself, so the leading `--` the CLI still deleted was a residual the seat wrote. Audited every separator site in brokkr-cli (git grep '"--"' -- crates/brokkr-cli/src returns seven hits and no eighth site: driver_extra_args, the hands box's own command boundary, four init.rs scaffold strings, recipes.rs's git clone terminator); the hands boundary is untouched and the shared helper keeps its body and its four callers. DSH opts out through a new driver_payload(kind, args). Proved through the BUILT CLI: 18 drives (bare, leading, interior, trailing terminators plus two bound-but-absent-route orderings) on each of disabled, enabled-cold and offered, each asserting the fixed option-terminator reason (never is_err), that the diagnostic echoes no model, route value, session id, `--` spelling or path, and that every provider observation is absent (no version probe, no child, no staged overlay, no retained root, no checkpoint) via an owned harmless shim and the admitted home. The bound-route cases also assert the error never says route_overlay. A companion test identifies each of the three paths by an observation only that path produces (0/1/1 probes; offered declines as resume_refusal unverified-harness), so the refusals cannot pass over an unrelated fixture. Removal proof run three times on the final tree: unit expectation failed `left: []` vs ["--"] at tests.rs:1186; built-CLI regression failed with the shim's own 'agent CLI exited 1' at driver_conformance.rs:370; with the route case reordered to the head, the same assertion failed naming 'route_overlay file is unreadable' from a leading terminator. Fix restored and all green. R2: the fixture canonicalizes each temporary root once, keeping its lifetime owner, before deriving workdir, shim, logs, DSH_HOME and operator HOME; the raw-path drive_dsh helper is gone. Other adapters proved unmoved by execution, not assertion: driver_conformance 22 passed including conformance_across_all_builtin_adapters and the codex rejoin proofs. Gates crate-scoped and sequential, all clean: fmt, workspace clippy, core 86, store 64, protocol 488, runtime 24 binaries, view 243, bridge 13, cli 32 binaries, both bundle compiles. OWED, not lowered: openspec validate --all --strict could not run in this seat under any spelling (the binary's directory is outside the seat's allowed paths); scripts/coverage-exact.sh needs a namespace the box refuses to nest; native macOS execution and remote CI on the final head are pending. Linux execution only. 8.8 and 8.10 stay unchecked, no sub-clause ticked; Pass C untouched and still owes the retained depth-zero header, the plugin's post-resume init event on the selected root, the absent fresh sibling root and sequence activity past firstSeq. No diff to contracts/, policy/, fixtures/, reference/, extensions/dsh/ or docs/decisions/; decision 0056 stays proposed; the DSH route stays disabled; no live provider was called.
